transcripts.transcript: Generative AI, also known as Gen AI, is an impressive technology. It's a kind of system that learns from texts, images and sounds made by real people to identify and reproduce particular traits of these works. This makes it able to create versions that are very similar to what people can do. But even for simple things like a pizza recipe, sometimes we might find some strange results. Of course we know glue as pizza topping is a wrong answer, but since AI doesn't think, it doesn't really know the difference. This example is based on real life events, and it shows how we need to be aware of the limitations of Gen AI. Although it can be a great help for creating text, images, or even sounds, these results need human supervision. This is because Gen AI is very good at identifying patterns, compressing information and trying to reconstruct it using statistics. But that only leads to an approximation of its sources because the AI cannot really think about it. But these systems can be very good at freeing up humans to focus on the real problems instead of getting stuck in boring activities. After all, the partnership between humans and machines through automation has always been about supervising and creating meaningful things with the help of technical agents who never get bored nor tired. However, the same things that make AI so exciting can also cause problems. After all, by creating statistical approximations of text, sound and images, we often get results that lack depth, nuance, diversity, or that are simply false. This is where the unreflective and unregulated usage of Gen AI becomes dangerous and a political issue. Just because something looks convincing doesn't mean it's true. Take deep fakes, for instance. It uses AI to change videos to make them look like a real person is doing or saying something they never did or said in real life. Gen AI can be used for disinformation campaigns to influence public opinion and elections. Tech companies behind these systems have a big influence on the public sphere and need proper regulations to preserve our democracy and respect human rights. Our individual actions can also help fight against disinformation. Because political processes are not as fast as the development of new technologies, it is crucial that everyone have critical AI competences, and the reason why Gen AI can be so good is because it is trained on the likelihood and works of real people who created books, songs, images and films. What sounds great at first comes with another ethical issue. The vast majority of these people weren't asked if they want to give away their original works to the companies who create and profit from these systems. And although the content created by AI is often generic and lacking in creativity and meaning. Some companies might be willing to sacrifice quality to become more profitable. This can negatively affect the jobs of countless workers in the creative sector, along with a decrease on the quality and creativity. In the end, AI systems are not just one thing, they have the power to both enrich and endanger our daily lives. If it's well regulated and accessible, AI can be a great tool to help us, but never to replace our creativity and critical thinking. What do you think are other potentials and threats of AI?
